arguments.text: Fixed. Interval.fromISO was calling DateTime.fromISO on both halves without guarding against throwOnInvalid, so the duration half threw before it could fall back to Duration.fromISO. It now probes each half safely and falls back to the duration parsing, so "2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00/PT5H30M" and "PT5H30M/2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00" both return the same valid interval as with the default setting. Genuinely unparsable input still throws InvalidIntervalError.

Fixed. objToLocalTS (src/impl/util.js) worked around Date.UTC's 19XX interpretation of years 0-99 by subtracting 1900 from the computed year, which resolves day overflow (e.g. 0099-12-31 + 61 days) in 19XX's leap-year structure (2000 is a leap year) instead of the target year's (100 is not). It now shifts the year by 400 (a full Gregorian cycle, identical leap structure) and shifts back, so DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 61 }).toISODate() === "0100-03-02".

Genuinely unparsable input still throws InvalidIntervalError.

It now shifts the year by 400 (a full Gregorian cycle, identical leap structure) and shifts back, so DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 61 }).toISODate() === "0100-03-02".

Fixed. isInDST compared the current offset against the offset at the same day-of-month in January and in May. In 1974 US DST began Jan 6, so for a January date the "January" probe landed on a DST day too and the comparison cancelled out. It now probes Jan 1 (which is standard time in 1974) and May, so dates in DST from Jan 6 onward report true, while winter dates still report false.

arguments.text: Fixed. The casual conversion matrix in src/duration.js was missing two entries (years.quarters and quarters.seconds), so normalize()/shiftTo()/as() divided by undefined and produced NaN whenever those pairs were combined. Added quarters: 4 to years and seconds: 91*24*60*60 to quarters (and quarters: 4 to years in the longterm matrix). Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 2 }).normalize().toObject() is now { years: 1, quarters: 2 } and { quarters: 1, seconds: 2 } stays { quarters: 1, seconds: 2 }.

Fixed. padStart (src/impl/util.js) padded the whole string including the minus sign, so -1 became "00-1". It now pads the absolute value and re-attaches the sign: year -1 => "-0001-01-01", year -10 => "-0010-01-01"; large negative years (-118040) and positive years are unchanged.

Fixed. FixedOffsetZone#isValid was hardcoded to true, so a zone built from a non-numeric offset was accepted. It now reports isNumber(this.fixed), and since the DateTime constructor already rejects invalid zones, DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: new FixedOffsetZone("CDT") }) is invalid with invalidReason "unsupported zone". Numeric fixed zones (including UTC) are unaffected.
